        <helpstring>{\rtf1\ansi\deff0{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Courier New;}}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\lang1044\f0\fs20 MODEL ABC2PHR
\par COMMENT
\par Calculates the real and imaginary part of a three-phase phasor. Magnitude not rms. 
\par Algorithm=0: 8-point RADIX-2 FFT algorithm for calculating phasor of specified frequency,
\par Algorithm=1: Recursive DFT algorithm. Faster, but more drift  
\par by Torstein Stadheim, 16.05.2012, and HKH Nov. 25, 2014
\par Source: Understanding Digital Signal Processing, Second Edition
\par         Richard G. Lyons, Prentice Hall, 2004,  Chapter 4    
\par ENDCOMMENT
\par 
\par DATA
\par   FREQ \{dflt:50\} -- Frequency of the first harmonic
\par   SampleFreq \{dflt:400\}
\par   Scale \{dflt:1\}
\par   Algorithm  \{dflt:0\}  --0: FFT8, 2:DFT recursive
\par INPUT
\par   x[1..3] -- The input signal which is to be analyzed
\par OUTPUT
\par   re[1..3]  -- Magnitude values of the fundamental frequency component. Phase ABC
\par   im[1..3]  -- Magnitude values of the fundamental frequency component. Phase ABC
\par VAR
\par   re[1..3], im[1..3],OMEGA,NSAMPL,alpha,D,i,delta_T[0..7]
\par   x1,x3,x5,x7,xre,xim
\par TIMESTEP min:recip(SampleFreq)
\par DELAY CELLS (X[1..3]): recip(FREQ*timestep)+2 -- Need at least one first harmonic periode of sampling
\par HISTORY X[1..3] \{DFLT:0\} -- Fills the signal with zeroes when time <= 0
\par INIT
\par   FOR i:= 0 TO 7 DO
\par     delta_T[i] := i/(FREQ*8)
\par   ENDFOR
\par   alpha:=1/sqrt(2)
\par   OMEGA:=2*PI*FREQ 
\par   NSAMPL:=recip(FREQ*timestep)
\par   if abs(NSAMPL-trunc(NSAMPL))>1e-9
\par   then
\par     write('%%%WARNING in ABC2PHR2: SAMPLEFREQ/FREQ is not an integer number')
\par   endif 
\par   re[1..3] :=0
\par   im[1..3] :=0
\par ENDINIT
\par EXEC
\par   for i:=1 to 3 do
\par     if Algorithm =0  --FFT Radix-2 8 levels
\par     then
\par       x1 := delay(x[i],delta_T[0],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[4],1)
\par       x3 := delay(x[i],delta_T[2],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[6],1)
\par       x5 := delay(x[i],delta_T[1],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[5],1)
\par       x7 := delay(x[i],delta_T[3],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[7],1)
\par       xre := x1 + (x5 - x7)*alpha
\par       xim := x3 + (x5 + x7)*alpha  
\par       re[i] := (xre*cos(OMEGA*T)+xim*sin(OMEGA*T))/4*Scale  --this moving window correction not needed in RX and PQ calc.
\par       im[i] := (xim*cos(OMEGA*T)-xre*sin(OMEGA*T))/4*Scale
\par     else  --DFT recursive moving window
\par       x7:=delay(X[i],1/FREQ,2)
\par       D:=2/NSAMPL*(X[i]-x7)*cos(OMEGA*T) 
\par       re[i]:=re[i]+D*Scale
\par       D:=2/NSAMPL*(X[i]-x7)*sin(OMEGA*T) 
\par       im[i]:=im[i]-D*Scale
\par     endif
\par   endfor
\par ENDEXEC
\par ENDMODEL
\par 
\par 
\par 
\par }
</helpstring>
        <datastring>MODEL ABC2PHRCOMMENTCalculates the real and imaginary part of a three-phase phasor. Magnitude not rms. Algorithm=0: 8-point RADIX-2 FFT algorithm for calculating phasor of specified frequency,Algorithm=1: Recursive DFT algorithm. Faster, but more drift  by Torstein Stadheim, 16.05.2012, and HKH Nov. 25, 2014Source: Understanding Digital Signal Processing, Second Edition        Richard G. Lyons, Prentice Hall, 2004,  Chapter 4    ENDCOMMENTDATA  FREQ {dflt:50} -- Frequency of the first harmonic  SampleFreq {dflt:400}  Scale {dflt:1}  Algorithm  {dflt:0}  --0: FFT8, 2:DFT recursiveINPUT  x[1..3] -- The input signal which is to be analyzedOUTPUT  re[1..3]  -- Magnitude values of the fundamental frequency component. Phase ABC  im[1..3]  -- Magnitude values of the fundamental frequency component. Phase ABCVAR  re[1..3], im[1..3],OMEGA,NSAMPL,alpha,D,i,delta_T[0..7]  x1,x3,x5,x7,xre,ximTIMESTEP min:recip(SampleFreq)DELAY CELLS (X[1..3]): recip(FREQ*timestep)+2 -- Need at least one first harmonic periode of samplingHISTORY X[1..3] {DFLT:0} -- Fills the signal with zeroes when time <= 0INIT  FOR i:= 0 TO 7 DO    delta_T[i] := i/(FREQ*8)  ENDFOR  alpha:=1/sqrt(2)  OMEGA:=2*PI*FREQ   NSAMPL:=recip(FREQ*timestep)  if abs(NSAMPL-trunc(NSAMPL))>1e-9  then    write('%%%WARNING in ABC2PHR2: SAMPLEFREQ/FREQ is not an integer number')  endif   re[1..3] :=0  im[1..3] :=0ENDINITEXEC  for i:=1 to 3 do    if Algorithm =0  --FFT Radix-2 8 levels    then      x1 := delay(x[i],delta_T[0],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[4],1)      x3 := delay(x[i],delta_T[2],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[6],1)      x5 := delay(x[i],delta_T[1],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[5],1)      x7 := delay(x[i],delta_T[3],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[7],1)      xre := x1 + (x5 - x7)*alpha      xim := x3 + (x5 + x7)*alpha        re[i] := (xre*cos(OMEGA*T)+xim*sin(OMEGA*T))/4*Scale  --this moving window correction not needed in RX and PQ calc.      im[i] := (xim*cos(OMEGA*T)-xre*sin(OMEGA*T))/4*Scale    else  --DFT recursive moving window      x7:=delay(X[i],1/FREQ,2)      D:=2/NSAMPL*(X[i]-x7)*cos(OMEGA*T)       re[i]:=re[i]+D*Scale      D:=2/NSAMPL*(X[i]-x7)*sin(OMEGA*T)       im[i]:=im[i]-D*Scale    endif  endforENDEXECENDMODEL</datastring>
      </comp_content>
      <Model UseAs="ABC2PHR" />
    </comp>

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\lang1044\f0\fs20 MODEL ABC2PHRF
\par COMMENT
\par 8-point RADIX-2 FFT algorithm for calculating phasor of specified or estimated frequency  
\par by HKH Nov. 25, 2014. Connect to a PLLQD model for frequency prediction.  
\par ENDCOMMENT
\par DATA
\par   FREQ \{dflt:50\} -- Frequency of the first harmonic
\par   SampleFreq \{dflt:400\}
\par   Scale \{dflt:1\}
\par INPUT
\par   x[1..3] -- The input signal which is to be analyzed
\par   FREQPLL \{DFLT:FREQ\}  --estimated frequency from a PLL block
\par   --Leave disconnected and unnamed to use data FREQ
\par OUTPUT
\par   re[1..3]  -- real part of the fundamental frequency component. Phase ABC. Peak not rms.
\par   im[1..3]  -- imaginary part of the fundamental frequency component. Phase ABC
\par VAR
\par   re[1..3], im[1..3],OMEGA,NSAMPL,alpha,i,delta_T[0..7]
\par   x1,x3,x5,x7,xre,xim
\par TIMESTEP min:recip(SampleFreq)
\par DELAY CELLS (X[1..3]): 2*recip(FREQ*timestep) -- Allow estimated freqpll be half of predefined freq
\par HISTORY X[1..3] \{DFLT:0\} -- Fills the signal with zeroes when time <= 0
\par INIT
\par   alpha:=1/sqrt(2)
\par ENDINIT
\par EXEC
\par   for i:= 0 to 7 do --since the frequency might change, new time delays must be calculated.
\par     delta_T[i] := i/(FREQPLL*8)
\par   endfor
\par   OMEGA:=2*PI*FREQPLL 
\par   for i:=1 to 3 do
\par     x1 := delay(x[i],delta_T[0],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[4],1)
\par     x3 := delay(x[i],delta_T[2],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[6],1)
\par     x5 := delay(x[i],delta_T[1],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[5],1)
\par     x7 := delay(x[i],delta_T[3],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[7],1)
\par     xre := x1 + (x5 - x7)*alpha
\par     xim := x3 + (x5 + x7)*alpha  
\par     re[i] := (xre*cos(OMEGA*T)+xim*sin(OMEGA*T))/4*Scale  
\par     im[i] := (xim*cos(OMEGA*T)-xre*sin(OMEGA*T))/4*Scale
\par   endfor
\par ENDEXEC
\par ENDMODEL
\par 
\par 
\par \pard 
\par }
</helpstring>

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\lang1044\b\f0\fs20 MODEL\cf0\b0  ABC2PHRH2
\par \cf2 comment-------------------------------------------------------------------
\par This model calculates the phasor in real and imaginary parts
\par of a time domain signal by a FFT/DFT algorithm in a moving window.
\par One period of the signal is needed to reach steady state.
\par The model outputs both the first and the h'th harmonic.
\par A Radix-2 16-level FFT method is hard coded for 1, 2 and 5th harmonic,
\par while a less accurate recursive DFT routine is used for other harmonics. 
\par SampleFreq frequency should be >16*FREQ, a whole facor of power frequency 
\par and whole fraction of 1/deltaT. 
\par The recursive DFT routine requires generally higher SampleFreq for accuracy.
\par HKH Dec. 12 2014.
\par ----------------------------------------------------------------endcomment\cf0 
\par \cf1\b INPUT\cf0\b0

        <datastring>MODEL ABC2PHRH2comment-------------------------------------------------------------------This model calculates the phasor in real and imaginary partsof a time domain signal by a FFT/DFT algorithm in a moving window.One period of the signal is needed to reach steady state.The model outputs both the first and the h'th harmonic.A Radix-2 16-level FFT method is hard coded for 1, 2 and 5th harmonic,while a less accurate recursive DFT routine is used for other harmonics. SampleFreq frequency should be >16*FREQ, a whole facor of power frequency and whole fraction of 1/deltaT. The recursive DFT routine requires generally higher SampleFreq for accuracy.HKH Dec. 12 2014.----------------------------------------------------------------endcommentINPUT   X[1..3]              --input signal to be transformedDATA    FREQ {DFLT:50}       --power frequency  h {dflt:2}           --other harmonic to output   scale {dflt:1}       --multiply output by this number  SampleFreq {dflt:800}--Sample frequency S/s should be >16*FREQOUTPUT   reF[1..3], imF[1..3]         --Fundamental phasor  reFh[1..3], imFh[1..3]       --h'th harmonic   VAR      reF[1..3], imF[1..3], reFh[1..3], imFh[1..3], NSAMPL, OMEGA  D,i, a,b,g,F1[0..3],F2[0..3],delta_T[0..15],n,dX[0..16],xre,ximHISTORY  X[1..3] {DFLT:0}TIMESTEP min:recip(SampleFreq)  DELAY CELLS (X[1..3]) : recip(FREQ*timestep)+2INIT   OMEGA:= 2*PI*FREQ  NSAMPL:=recip(FREQ*timestep)  reF[1..3] :=0  imF[1..3] :=0  reFh[1..3] :=0  imFh[1..3] :=0  a:=cos(pi/8)  b:=sin(pi/8)  g:=1/sqrt(2)  for n:=0 to 15 do    delta_T[n]:=n*recip(FREQ*16)  endforENDINITEXEC  FOR i:=1 TO 3 DO    for n:=0 to 15 do      dX[n]:=delay(X[i],delta_T[n],1)    endfor    --1st harmonic FFT radix-2 16 level    xRe:=dX[0]-dX[8]+a*(dX[1]-dX[9]-dX[7]+dX[15])    xRe:=xRe+g*(dX[2]-dX[10]-dX[6]+dX[14])+b*(dX[3]-dX[11]-dX[5]+dX[13])    xIm:=dX[4]-dX[12]+b*(dX[1]-dX[9]+dX[7]-dX[15])    xIm:=xIm+g*(dX[2]-dX[10]+dX[6]-dX[14])+a*(dX[3]-dX[11]+dX[5]-dX[13])    reF[i] := (xre*cos(OMEGA*T)+xim*sin(OMEGA*T))/8*Scale      imF[i] := (xim*cos(OMEGA*T)-xre*sin(OMEGA*T))/8*Scale    if h=2 then      --2nd harmonic FFT radix-2 16 level      xRe:=dX[0]+dX[8]-dX[4]-dX[12]      xRe:=xRe+g*(dX[1]-dX[3]-dX[5]+dX[7]+dX[9]-dX[11]-dX[13]+dX[15])      xIm:=dX[2]-dX[6]+dX[10]-dX[14]      xIm:=xIm+g*(dX[1]+dX[3]-dX[5]-dX[7]+dX[9]+dX[11]-dX[13]-dX[15])      reFh[i] := (xre*cos(2*OMEGA*T)+xim*sin(2*OMEGA*T))/8*Scale        imFh[i] := (xim*cos(2*OMEGA*T)-xre*sin(2*OMEGA*T))/8*Scale    elsif h=5 then      --5th harmonic FFT radix-2 16 level      xRe:=dX[0]-dX[8]-b*(dX[1]-dX[9]-dX[7]+dX[15])      xRe:=xRe-g*(dX[2]-dX[10]-dX[6]+dX[14])+a*(dX[3]-dX[11]-dX[5]+dX[13])      xIm:=dX[4]-dX[12]+a*(dX[1]-dX[9]+dX[7]-dX[15])      xIm:=xIm-g*(dX[2]-dX[10]+dX[6]-dX[14])-b*(dX[3]-dX[11]+dX[5]-dX[13])      reFh[i] := (xre*cos(5*OMEGA*T)+xim*sin(5*OMEGA*T))/8*Scale        imFh[i] := (xim*cos(5*OMEGA*T)-xre*sin(5*OMEGA*T))/8*Scale    else      --less accurate, but general recursive DFT method      dX[16]:=delay(X[i],1/FREQ,2)      D:=2/NSAMPL*(X[i]-dX[16])*cos(h*OMEGA*T)       reFh[i]:=reFh[i]+D*Scale      D:=2/NSAMPL*(X[i]-dX[16])*sin(h*OMEGA*T)       imFh[i]:=imFh[i]-D*Scale    endif   ENDFORENDEXECENDMODEL</datastring>

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\lang1044\f0\fs20 MODEL ABC2PHRI
\par comment---------------------------------------------------------------------
\par The model calculates the phasor of the input voltage with initial conditions.
\par Downsampling and algorithm selection.
\par ------------------------------------------------------------------endcomment
\par 
\par INPUT 
\par   X[1..3]        --Input signal to be transformed
\par   Xim[1..3]      --Imaginary part of steady-state signal (real part is X)   
\par DATA  
\par   FREQ \{DFLT:50\}        --Power frequency 
\par   SampleFreq \{DFLT:400\} --Sample frequency S/s
\par   Algorithm \{dflt:0\}    --0:FFT Radix 2-8, 1: DFT recursive
\par OUTPUT 
\par   reX[1..3],imX[1..3]   --Phasor
\par VAR    
\par   reX[1..3], imX[1..3],j,OMEGA,NSAMPL,D,alpha,x1,x3,x5,x7,xR,xI,delta_T[0..7]
\par TIMESTEP min: recip(SampleFreq)
\par DELAY CELLS (X[1..3]): recip(FREQ*timestep)+2
\par INIT
\par   OMEGA:= 2*PI*FREQ
\par   NSAMPL:=recip(FREQ*timestep)
\par   for j:=1 to 3 do
\par     reX[j]:=X[j]
\par     imX[j]:=Xim[j]
\par   endfor
\par   alpha:=1/sqrt(2) 
\par   for j:= 0 to 7 do
\par     delta_T[j] := j/(FREQ*8)
\par   endfor  
\par ENDINIT
\par HISTORY
\par   X[1] \{DFLT:sqrt(reX[1]**2+imX[1]**2)*cos(t*omega+atan2(imX[1],reX[1]))\}
\par   X[2] \{DFLT:sqrt(reX[2]**2+imX[2]**2)*cos(t*omega+atan2(imx[2],reX[2]))\}
\par   X[3] \{DFLT:sqrt(reX[3]**2+imX[3]**2)*cos(t*omega+atan2(imX[3],reX[3]))\}
\par EXEC
\par   for j:=1 to 3 do
\par     if Algorithm=0
\par     then
\par       x1 := delay(X[j],delta_T[0],2) - delay(X[j],delta_T[4],2)
\par       x3 := delay(X[j],delta_T[2],2) - delay(X[j],delta_T[6],2)
\par       x5 := delay(X[j],delta_T[1],2) - delay(X[j],delta_T[5],2)
\par       x7 := delay(X[j],delta_T[3],2) - delay(X[j],delta_T[7],2)
\par       xR := x1 + (x5 - x7)*alpha
\par       xI := x3 + (x5 + x7)*alpha
\par       reX[j] := (xR*cos(OMEGA*T)+xI*sin(OMEGA*T))/4
\par       imX[j] := (xI*cos(OMEGA*T)-xR*sin(OMEGA*T))/4
\par     else
\par       x1:=delay(X[j],1/FREQ,2)
\par       D:=2/NSAMPL*(X[j]-x1)*cos(OMEGA*T) 
\par       reX[j]:=reX[j]+D
\par       D:=2/NSAMPL*(X[j]-x1)*sin(OMEGA*T) 
\par       imX[j]:=imX[j]-D
\par     endif
\par   endfor
\par ENDEXEC
\par ENDMODEL
\par 
\par \pard 
\par }

        <datastring>MODEL ABC2PHRIcomment---------------------------------------------------------------------The model calculates the phasor of the input voltage with initial conditions.Downsampling and algorithm selection.------------------------------------------------------------------endcommentINPUT   X[1..3]        --Input signal to be transformed  Xim[1..3]      --Imaginary part of steady-state signal (real part is X)   DATA    FREQ {DFLT:50}        --Power frequency   SampleFreq {DFLT:400} --Sample frequency S/s  Algorithm {dflt:0}    --0:FFT Radix 2-8, 1: DFT recursiveOUTPUT   reX[1..3],imX[1..3]   --PhasorVAR      reX[1..3], imX[1..3],j,OMEGA,NSAMPL,D,alpha,x1,x3,x5,x7,xR,xI,delta_T[0..7]TIMESTEP min: recip(SampleFreq)DELAY CELLS (X[1..3]): recip(FREQ*timestep)+2INIT  OMEGA:= 2*PI*FREQ  NSAMPL:=recip(FREQ*timestep)  for j:=1 to 3 do    reX[j]:=X[j]    imX[j]:=Xim[j]  endfor  alpha:=1/sqrt(2)   for j:= 0 to 7 do    delta_T[j] := j/(FREQ*8)  endfor  ENDINITHISTORY  X[1] {DFLT:sqrt(reX[1]**2+imX[1]**2)*cos(t*omega+atan2(imX[1],reX[1]))}  X[2] {DFLT:sqrt(reX[2]**2+imX[2]**2)*cos(t*omega+atan2(imx[2],reX[2]))}  X[3] {DFLT:sqrt(reX[3]**2+imX[3]**2)*cos(t*omega+atan2(imX[3],reX[3]))}EXEC  for j:=1 to 3 do    if Algorithm=0    then      x1 := delay(X[j],delta_T[0],2) - delay(X[j],delta_T[4],2)      x3 := delay(X[j],delta_T[2],2) - delay(X[j],delta_T[6],2)      x5 := delay(X[j],delta_T[1],2) - delay(X[j],delta_T[5],2)      x7 := delay(X[j],delta_T[3],2) - delay(X[j],delta_T[7],2)      xR := x1 + (x5 - x7)*alpha      xI := x3 + (x5 + x7)*alpha      reX[j] := (xR*cos(OMEGA*T)+xI*sin(OMEGA*T))/4      imX[j] := (xI*cos(OMEGA*T)-xR*sin(OMEGA*T))/4    else      x1:=delay(X[j],1/FREQ,2)      D:=2/NSAMPL*(X[j]-x1)*cos(OMEGA*T)       reX[j]:=reX[j]+D      D:=2/NSAMPL*(X[j]-x1)*sin(OMEGA*T)       imX[j]:=imX[j]-D    endif  endforENDEXECENDMODEL</datastring>

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\lang1044\f0\fs20 MODEL ABC2RMS
\par comment------------------------------------------------------------------
\par Calculates the true rms value of a 3-phase signal based on integration.
\par SampleFreq frequency should be whole multiple of power frequency.
\par ---------------------------------------------------------------endcomment
\par DATA   
\par   freq          -- base frequency
\par   xrms_ini \{dflt:-1\} -- initial rms value
\par   scale \{dflt:1\} --multiply output by this number 
\par   SampleFreq     -- sample frequency in Hz
\par INPUT  
\par   x[1..3]        -- monitored signal
\par OUTPUT 
\par   xrms[1..3]     -- rms value of monitored signal
\par VAR    
\par   xrms[1..3]     
\par   x2[1..3]       -- internal, x*x
\par   ix2[1..3]      -- internal, integral of x2
\par   period         -- 1/freq
\par   n
\par TIMESTEP min:recip(SampleFreq) --this restricts local timestep to avoid overflow
\par DELAY CELLS(ix2[1..3]): recip(freq*timestep) +2
\par INIT
\par   period       := recip(freq)
\par   histdef(ix2[1..3]) := 0
\par   integral(x2[1..3]) := 0
\par   IF xrms_ini <0 THEN xrms[1..3]:=0 ELSE xrms[1..3]:=xrms_ini ENDIF
\par ENDINIT
\par EXEC
\par   FOR n:=1 TO 3 DO
\par     x2[n]  := x[n]*x[n]
\par     ix2[n] := integral(x2[n])
\par     IF t>period THEN
\par       xrms[n] := sqrt((ix2[n] - delay(ix2[n], period))*freq)*scale
\par     ENDIF
\par   ENDFOR
\par ENDEXEC
\par ENDMODEL
\par 
\par \pard 
\par 
\par }
</helpstring>
        <datastring>MODEL ABC2RMScomment------------------------------------------------------------------Calculates the true rms value of a 3-phase signal based on integration.SampleFreq frequency should be whole multiple of power frequency.---------------------------------------------------------------endcommentDATA     freq          -- base frequency  xrms_ini {dflt:-1} -- initial rms value  scale {dflt:1} --multiply output by this number   SampleFreq     -- sample frequency in HzINPUT    x[1..3]        -- monitored signalOUTPUT   xrms[1..3]     -- rms value of monitored signalVAR      xrms[1..3]       x2[1..3]       -- internal, x*x  ix2[1..3]      -- internal, integral of x2  period         -- 1/freq  nTIMESTEP min:recip(SampleFreq) --this restricts local timestep to avoid overflowDELAY CELLS(ix2[1..3]): recip(freq*timestep) +2INIT  period       := recip(freq)  histdef(ix2[1..3]) := 0  integral(x2[1..3]) := 0  IF xrms_ini <0 THEN xrms[1..3]:=0 ELSE xrms[1..3]:=xrms_ini ENDIFENDINITEXEC  FOR n:=1 TO 3 DO    x2[n]  := x[n]*x[n]    ix2[n] := integral(x2[n])    IF t>period THEN      xrms[n] := sqrt((ix2[n] - delay(ix2[n], period))*freq)*scale    ENDIF  ENDFORENDEXECENDMODEL</datastring>
      </comp_content>

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\lang1044\f0\fs20 MODEL ABC2SEQ
\par COMMENT
\par Calculates the real and imaginary part of a three-phase phasor. Magnitude not rms. 
\par Algorithm=0: 8-point RADIX-2 FFT algorithm for calculating phasor of specified frequency,
\par Algorithm=1: Recursive DFT algorithm. Faster, but more drift  
\par by Torstein Stadheim, 16.05.2012, and HKH Nov. 25, 2014
\par Source: Understanding Digital Signal Processing, Second Edition
\par         Richard G. Lyons, Prentice Hall, 2004,  Chapter 4    
\par ENDCOMMENT
\par 
\par DATA
\par   FREQ \{dflt:50\} -- Frequency of the first harmonic
\par   SampleFreq \{dflt:400\}
\par   Scale \{dflt:1\}
\par   Algorithm  \{dflt:0\}  --0: FFT8, 2:DFT recursive
\par INPUT
\par   x[1..3] -- The input signal which is to be analyzed
\par OUTPUT
\par   SEQre[1..3]  -- Real part of fundamental sequence components 0-1-2
\par   SEQim[1..3]  -- Imaginary part of fundamental sequence components 0-1-2
\par VAR
\par   SEQre[1..3],SEQim[1..3],re[1..3], im[1..3],OMEGA,NSAMPL,alpha,D,i,delta_T[0..7]
\par   x1,x3,x5,x7,xre,xim
\par TIMESTEP min:recip(SampleFreq)
\par DELAY CELLS (X[1..3]): recip(FREQ*timestep)+2 -- Need at least one first harmonic periode of sampling
\par HISTORY X[1..3] \{DFLT:0\} -- Fills the signal with zeroes when time <= 0
\par INIT
\par   FOR i:= 0 TO 7 DO
\par     delta_T[i] := i/(FREQ*8)
\par   ENDFOR
\par   alpha:=1/sqrt(2)
\par   OMEGA:=2*PI*FREQ 
\par   NSAMPL:=recip(FREQ*timestep)
\par   if abs(NSAMPL-trunc(NSAMPL))>1e-9
\par   then
\par     write('%%%WARNING in ABC2SEQ: SAMPLEFREQ/FREQ is not an integer number')
\par   endif 
\par   re[1..3] :=0
\par   im[1..3] :=0
\par ENDINIT
\par EXEC
\par   for i:=1 to 3 do
\par     if Algorithm =0  --FFT Radix-2 8 levels
\par     then
\par       x1 := delay(x[i],delta_T[0],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[4],1)
\par       x3 := delay(x[i],delta_T[2],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[6],1)
\par       x5 := delay(x[i],delta_T[1],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[5],1)
\par       x7 := delay(x[i],delta_T[3],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[7],1)
\par       xre := x1 + (x5 - x7)*alpha
\par       xim := x3 + (x5 + x7)*alpha  
\par       re[i] := (xre*cos(OMEGA*T)+xim*sin(OMEGA*T))/4*Scale  --this moving window correction not needed in RX and PQ calc.
\par       im[i] := (xim*cos(OMEGA*T)-xre*sin(OMEGA*T))/4*Scale
\par     else  --DFT recursive moving window
\par       x7:=delay(X[i],1/FREQ,2)
\par       D:=2/NSAMPL*(X[i]-x7)*cos(OMEGA*T) 
\par       re[i]:=re[i]+D*Scale
\par       D:=2/NSAMPL*(X[i]-x7)*sin(OMEGA*T) 
\par       im[i]:=im[i]-D*Scale
\par     endif
\par   endfor
\par   SEQre[1]:=1/3*(re[1]+re[2]+re[3])  --0 zero
\par   SEQim[1]:=1/3*(im[1]+im[2]+im[3])
\par   SEQre[2]:=1/3*(re[1]-0.5*re[2]-0.5*re[3]-sqrt(3)/2*(im[2]-im[3]))  --1 pos
\par   SEQim[2]:=1/3*(im[1]-0.5*im[2]-0.5*im[3]+sqrt(3)/2*(re[2]-re[3]))
\par   SEQre[3]:=1/3*(re[1]-0.5*re[2]-0.5*re[3]+sqrt(3)/2*(im[2]-im[3]))  --2 neg
\par   SEQim[3]:=1/3*(im[1]-0.5*im[2]-0.5*im[3]-sqrt(3)/2*(re[2]-re[3]))
\par ENDEXEC
\par ENDMODEL
\par }
</helpstring>
        <datastring>MODEL ABC2SEQCOMMENTCalculates the real and imaginary part of a three-phase phasor. Magnitude not rms. Algorithm=0: 8-point RADIX-2 FFT algorithm for calculating phasor of specified frequency,Algorithm=1: Recursive DFT algorithm. Faster, but more drift  by Torstein Stadheim, 16.05.2012, and HKH Nov. 25, 2014Source: Understanding Digital Signal Processing, Second Edition        Richard G. Lyons, Prentice Hall, 2004,  Chapter 4    ENDCOMMENTDATA  FREQ {dflt:50} -- Frequency of the first harmonic  SampleFreq {dflt:400}  Scale {dflt:1}  Algorithm  {dflt:0}  --0: FFT8, 2:DFT recursiveINPUT  x[1..3] -- The input signal which is to be analyzedOUTPUT  SEQre[1..3]  -- Real part of fundamental sequence components 0-1-2  SEQim[1..3]  -- Imaginary part of fundamental sequence components 0-1-2VAR  SEQre[1..3],SEQim[1..3],re[1..3], im[1..3],OMEGA,NSAMPL,alpha,D,i,delta_T[0..7]  x1,x3,x5,x7,xre,ximTIMESTEP min:recip(SampleFreq)DELAY CELLS (X[1..3]): recip(FREQ*timestep)+2 -- Need at least one first harmonic periode of samplingHISTORY X[1..3] {DFLT:0} -- Fills the signal with zeroes when time <= 0INIT  FOR i:= 0 TO 7 DO    delta_T[i] := i/(FREQ*8)  ENDFOR  alpha:=1/sqrt(2)  OMEGA:=2*PI*FREQ   NSAMPL:=recip(FREQ*timestep)  if abs(NSAMPL-trunc(NSAMPL))>1e-9  then    write('%%%WARNING in ABC2SEQ: SAMPLEFREQ/FREQ is not an integer number')  endif   re[1..3] :=0  im[1..3] :=0ENDINITEXEC  for i:=1 to 3 do    if Algorithm =0  --FFT Radix-2 8 levels    then      x1 := delay(x[i],delta_T[0],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[4],1)      x3 := delay(x[i],delta_T[2],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[6],1)      x5 := delay(x[i],delta_T[1],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[5],1)      x7 := delay(x[i],delta_T[3],1) - delay(x[i],delta_T[7],1)      xre := x1 + (x5 - x7)*alpha      xim := x3 + (x5 + x7)*alpha        re[i] := (xre*cos(OMEGA*T)+xim*sin(OMEGA*T))/4*Scale  --this moving window correction not needed in RX and PQ calc.      im[i] := (xim*cos(OMEGA*T)-xre*sin(OMEGA*T))/4*Scale    else  --DFT recursive moving window      x7:=delay(X[i],1/FREQ,2)      D:=2/NSAMPL*(X[i]-x7)*cos(OMEGA*T)       re[i]:=re[i]+D*Scale      D:=2/NSAMPL*(X[i]-x7)*sin(OMEGA*T)       im[i]:=im[i]-D*Scale    endif  endfor  SEQre[1]:=1/3*(re[1]+re[2]+re[3])  --0 zero  SEQim[1]:=1/3*(im[1]+im[2]+im[3])  SEQre[2]:=1/3*(re[1]-0.5*re[2]-0.5*re[3]-sqrt(3)/2*(im[2]-im[3]))  --1 pos  SEQim[2]:=1/3*(im[1]-0.5*im[2]-0.5*im[3]+sqrt(3)/2*(re[2]-re[3]))  SEQre[3]:=1/3*(re[1]-0.5*re[2]-0.5*re[3]+sqrt(3)/2*(im[2]-im[3]))  --2 neg  SEQim[3]:=1/3*(im[1]-0.5*im[2]-0.5*im[3]-sqrt(3)/2*(re[2]-re[3]))ENDEXECENDMODEL</datastring>
      </comp_content>
      <Model UseAs="ABC2SEQ" />
    </comp>

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\lang1044\f0\fs20 MODEL BHPFILT
\par comment-----------------------------------------------
\par Butterworth high pass filter order 0-3
\par Amplitude corrected for specified frequency ScaleFreq
\par --------------------------------------------endcomment
\par DATA   
\par   Gain        \{dflt:1\}   --gain of filter
\par   FilterFreq  \{dflt:800\} --high pass filter frequency
\par   FilterOrder \{dflt:2\}   --Order of Butterworth filter 0..3
\par   ScaleFreq   \{dflt:50\}  --Base frequency for scaling. 0=no scale
\par INPUT  
\par   X[1..3]        -- monitored signal
\par OUTPUT 
\par   XF[1..3]       -- filtered signal
\par VAR    
\par   XF[1..3],tau,n,alpha,beta,amp,arg
\par HISTORY xf[1..3] \{dflt:0\}
\par INIT
\par   tau:=recip(2*PI*FilterFreq)
\par   beta:=ScaleFreq*recip(FilterFreq)
\par   --calculate amplitude scaling at power frequency
\par   if beta=0 then
\par     alpha:=Gain
\par   else
\par     alpha:=Gain*sqrt((1+beta**(2*FilterOrder)))*recip(beta**FilterOrder)
\par   endif
\par ENDINIT  
\par EXEC
\par   FOR n:=1 TO 3 DO
\par     if FilterOrder=1 then
\par       claplace(XF[n]/X[n]):=(alpha*tau|s1)/(1|s0+tau|s1)
\par     elsif FilterOrder=2 then
\par       claplace(XF[n]/X[n]):=(alpha*tau**2|s2)/(1|s0+sqrt(2)*tau|s1+tau**2|s2)
\par     elsif FilterOrder=3 then
\par       claplace(XF[n]/X[n]):=(alpha*tau**3|s3)/(1|s0+2*tau|s1+2*tau**2|s2+tau**3|s3)
\par     else
\par       XF[n]:=Gain*X[n] 
\par     endif
\par   ENDFOR
\par ENDEXEC
\par ENDMODEL
\par 
\par 
\par 
\par 
\par 
\par 
\par }
</helpstring>

EXTRACT1.plantilla:
<comp Name="EXTRACT1" Id="EXTRACT1">
      <comp_content HighRes="false" Icon="default">
        <node Name="X" Value="" Kind="1" PosX="-20" PosY="0" NamePosX="-4" NamePosY="0" />
        <data Name="AsFuncOf" Unit="Var" Value="1" />
        <data Name="Scale" Unit="Divide" Value="1" />
        <data Name="MinMaxAbs" Unit="1/0; 1=Max" Value="1" />
        <data Name="TStart" Unit="s" Value="0" />
        <data Name="TStop" Unit="s" Value="100" />
        <data Name="OnScreen" Unit="0..NumSim" Value="1" />
        <data Name="Digits" Unit="resolution" Value="7" />
        <data Name="Idx" Unit="ATPDraw" Value="0" />
        <datastring>MODEL EXTRACT1
comment--------------------------------------------------------
| Special purpose Model.                                      |
| The output of this Model is written to the lis-file.        |
| The data Idx is used to identify the module in the lis-file.|
| The lis-file is automatically read after the simulation.    |
| Handles multiple run. If AsFuncOf is a number the           |
| simulation number is used instead.                          | 
-----------------------------------------------------endcomment
INPUT X
DATA 
  AsFuncOf --specify variable for x-axis plotting, otherwise KNT is used  
  Scale --this can be an Variable. Used in the plotting x-axis
  MinMaxAbs --0: capture minimum, 1: maximum, 2: maximum absolute 
  Tstart   --wait until this time to start looking for an extreme value.
  Tstop    --stop looking for extreme value after this time
  OnScreen --<=0 nothing to screen. >0 is the simulation number KNT to plot
  Digits   --On screen resolution
  Idx      --unique identifier (managed by ATPDraw)
VAR xmin,xmax,xout,y,out
INIT
  xout:=0
  xmin:=inf
  xmax:=-inf
  out:=true;
ENDINIT
EXEC
  if T>=Tstart
  then
    y:=x
    if MinMaxAbs=2
    then
      y:=abs(x)
    endif  
    xmin:=min(xmin,y)
    xmax:=max(xmax,y)
    if MinMaxAbs>0
    then
      xout:=xmax
    else 
      xout:=xmin
    endif
  endif
  if out and ((T>=Tstop ) or (round(T/timestep)=round(stoptime/timestep)))
  then 
    write('BEGIN WRITE @EXTRACT1',trunc(Idx))    --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw
    write(xout*recip(Scale),' ',AsFuncOf)                        --Add multiple columns or multiple lines 
    write('END WRITE @EXTRACT1',trunc(Idx))      --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw
    out:=false;  
  endif
ENDEXEC
ENDMODEL </datastring>
      </comp_content>
      <Model UseAs="EXTRACT1" />
    </comp>

        <datastring>MODEL EXTRACT3
comment--------------------------------------------------------
| Special purpose Model.                                      |
| The output of this Model is written to the lis-file.        |
| The data Idx is used to identify the module in the lis-file.|
| The lis-file is automatically read after the simulation.    |
| Handles multiple run. If AsFuncOf is a number the           |
| simulation number is used instead.                          | 
-----------------------------------------------------endcomment
INPUT X[1..3]
DATA 
  AsFuncOf --specify variable for x-axis plotting, otherwise KNT is used  
  Scale --this can be an Variable. Used in the plotting x-axis
  MinMaxAbs --0: capture minimum, 1: maximum, 2: maximum absolute 
  Tstart   --wait until this time to start looking for an extreme value.
  Tstop    --stop looking for extreme value after this time
  OnScreen --<=0 nothing to screen. >0 is the simulation number KNT to plot
  Digits   --On screen resolution
  Idx      --unique identifier (managed by ATPDraw)
VAR xmin[1..3],xmax[1..3],xout[1..3],y[1..3],out,i
INIT
  xout[1..3]:=0
  xmin[1..3]:=inf
  xmax[1..3]:=-inf
  out:=true;
ENDINIT
EXEC
  if T>=Tstart
  then
    for i:=1 to 3 do    
      y[i]:=x[i]
      if MinMaxAbs=2
      then
        y[i]:=abs(x[i])
      endif  
      xmin[i]:=min(xmin[i],y[i])
      xmax[i]:=max(xmax[i],y[i])
      if MinMaxAbs>0
      then
        xout[i]:=xmax[i]
      else 
        xout[i]:=xmin[i]
      endif
    endfor
  endif
  if out and ((T>=Tstop ) or (round(T/timestep)=round(stoptime/timestep)))
  then
    for i:=1 to 3 do
      xout[i]:=xout[i]*recip(Scale)
    endfor
    write('BEGIN WRITE @EXTRACT3',trunc(Idx))    --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw
    write(xout[1],' ',xout[2],' ',xout[3], ' ',AsFuncOf) --Add multiple columns or multiple lines 
    write('END WRITE @EXTRACT3',trunc(Idx))      --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw
    out:=false;  
  endif

            <datastring>MODEL LOADPQG
comment------------------------------------------------------------
The model calculates the phasor of the input voltage and outputs a
current so that the active and reactive power becomes as given by
the user with an exponential voltage dependency.
NP=0: Constant power
NP=1: Contant current
NP=2: Constant impedance
The model in the LOAD model of ATPDraw group together with a current 
source and a steady-state impedance.
----------------------------------------------------------endcomment

INPUT V[1..3]        --Input signal to be transformed
      Vim[1..3]      --Imaginary part of steady-state voltage phase A (real part is V[1])   
DATA  FREQ {DFLT:50} --Power frequency 
      UN, PN, QN, NP, NQ
OUTPUT I[1..3]       --Load current
VAR    I[1..3],absV[1..3], angV[1..3],reV[1..3], imV[1..3],j,NSAMPL,OMEGA
       D,F1,F2,F3,F4,Kp,Kq,A,b

DELAY CELLS (V[1..3]): 1/(FREQ*timestep)+1

INIT 
  OMEGA:= 2*PI*FREQ
  NSAMPL:=1/(FREQ*timestep)
  FOR j:=1 to 3 DO
    reV[j]:=V[j]
    imV[j]:=Vim[j]
    absV[j]:=sqrt(Vim[j]**2+V[j]**2)
    angV[j]:=atan2(Vim[j],V[j])
  ENDFOR
  --UN:=UN*1e3/sqrt(3)     --Work with phase quantities
  Kp:=PN*1e6/((UN*1e3/sqrt(3/2))**NP)    --Voltage V as phase voltage
  Kq:=QN*1e6/((UN*1e3/sqrt(3/2))**NQ)                               
ENDINIT
HISTORY
  V[1] {DFLT:(absV[1])*cos(t*omega+angV[1])}
  V[2] {DFLT:(absV[2])*cos(t*omega+angV[2])}
  V[3] {DFLT:(absV[3])*cos(t*omega+angV[3])}
EXEC
  FOR j:=1 to 3 DO
    f1:=delay(V[j],(NSAMPL+1)*timestep,1)
    f2:=delay(V[j],NSAMPL*timestep,1)
    f3:=delay(V[j],timestep,1)
    f4:=V[j]
  
    D:=1/PI*((f4-f2)*sin(OMEGA*T)-(f3-f1)*sin(OMEGA*(T-timestep))
       +(f4-f3-f2+f1)/(timestep*OMEGA)*
       (cos(OMEGA*T)-cos(OMEGA*(T-timestep)))) 

    reV[j]:=reV[j]+D
    
    D:=1/PI*((f4-f2)*cos(OMEGA*T)-(f3-f1)*cos(OMEGA*(T-timestep))
       -(f4-f3-f2+f1)/(timestep*OMEGA)*
       (sin(OMEGA*T)-sin(OMEGA*(T-timestep)))) 

    imV[j]:=imV[j]+D
    absV[j]:=sqrt(reV[j]**2+imV[j]**2)
    angV[j]:=atan2(imV[j],reV[j]) 
    A:=sqrt((Kp*absV[j]**(NP-1))**2+(Kq*absV[j]**(NQ-1))**2 )
    b:=angV[j]-atan2(Kq*absV[j]**NQ,Kp*absV[j]**NP)
    I[j]:=-A*cos(OMEGA*(T+timestep)+b)*2/3                                     
  ENDFOR 
ENDEXEC
ENDMODEL
</datastring>

absV[3] AS absV3</Model>

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\lang1044\f0\fs20 MODEL HARMONICS
\par comment----------------------------------------------------
\par This model calculates the harmonics up to maximum order 26
\par of a time varying signal X based on a DFT algorithm in a 
\par moving window. Scale=1; output of peak quantities. 
\par -------------------------------------------------endcomment
\par INPUT X                    --input signal to be transformed
\par DATA  FREQ \{DFLT:50\}       --power frequency
\par       n \{DFLT:26\}          --number of harmonics to calculate     
\par       Scale \{DFLT:1\}       --scaling of the harmonics values
\par OUTPUT absH[1..26], angH[1..26],H0 --Harmonic outputs. H0 is DC comp.
\par VAR    absH[1..26], angH[1..26],H0,reH[1..26], imH[1..26],i,NSAMPL,OMEGA
\par        D,F1,F2,F3,F4
\par 
\par HISTORY
\par   X \{DFLT:0\}
\par   
\par DELAY CELLS DFLT: 1/(FREQ*timestep)+1
\par 
\par INIT 
\par   OMEGA:= 2*PI*FREQ
\par   NSAMPL:=1/(FREQ*timestep)
\par   H0:=0
\par   FOR i:=1 to 26 DO
\par     reH[i]:=0
\par     imH[i]:=0
\par     absH[i]:=0
\par     angH[i]:=0
\par   ENDFOR
\par ENDINIT
\par EXEC
\par   f1:=delay(X,(NSAMPL+1)*timestep,1)
\par   f2:=delay(X,NSAMPL*timestep,1)
\par   f3:=delay(X,timestep,1)
\par   f4:=X
\par   H0:=H0+(f4+f3-f2-f1)/(2*NSAMPL)
\par   FOR i:=1 to n DO
\par     D:=1/(i*PI)*((f4-f2)*sin(i*OMEGA*T)-(f3-f1)*sin(i*OMEGA*(T-timestep))
\par        +(f4-f3-f2+f1)/(timestep*i*OMEGA)*
\par        (cos(i*OMEGA*T)-cos(i*OMEGA*(T-timestep)))) 
\par     reH[i]:=reH[i]+D
\par     
\par     D:=1/(i*PI)*((f4-f2)*cos(i*OMEGA*T)-(f3-f1)*cos(i*OMEGA*(T-timestep))
\par        -(f4-f3-f2+f1)/(timestep*i*OMEGA)*
\par        (sin(i*OMEGA*T)-sin(i*OMEGA*(T-timestep)))) 
\par     imH[i]:=imH[i]+D
\par     
\par     absH[i]:=sqrt(reH[i]**2+imH[i]**2)*Scale
\par     IF abs(imH[i])<1E-10
\par     THEN
\par       angH[i]:=0
\par     ELSE
\par       angH[i]:=atan2(imH[i],reH[i]) 
\par     ENDIF
\par   ENDFOR 
\par 
\par ENDEXEC
\par ENDMODEL
\par 
\par }
</helpstring>

MODEL.plantilla:
<comp Name="MODEL" Id="FLASH_1">
      <comp_content HighRes="false" Icon="bitmap">
        <node Name="V1" Value="" Kind="2" PosX="-20" PosY="-10" NamePosX="4" NamePosY="-4" />
        <node Name="V2" Value="" Kind="2" PosX="-20" PosY="0" NamePosX="4" NamePosY="-4" />
        <node Name="iczn" Value="" Kind="2" PosX="-20" PosY="10" NamePosX="4" NamePosY="-4" />
        <node Name="trip" Value="" PosX="20" PosY="0" NamePosX="4" NamePosY="-4" />
        <data Name="Pset" Unit="" Value="0" />
        <data Name="Eset" Unit="" Value="0" />
        <data Name="fdel" Unit="" Value="0" />
        <data Name="fdur" Unit="" Value="0" />
        <icon BRectTop="-20" BRectLeft="-20" BRectBottom="20" BRectRight="20" ExtPX="0" ExtPY="0"></icon>
        <datastring>MODEL FLASH_1

comment ****************************************************************
*                                                                      *
*    Function: set or cancel the gap firing control signal             *
*    Inputs  : voltage and current across ZnO resistor                 *
*    Output  : the firing signal to the electrical ZnO component       *
*                                                                      *
************************************************************* endcomment

  INPUT  V1     --  Voltage on positive side of ZNO        [V]
         V2     --  Voltage of negative side of ZNO        [V]
         iczn   --  ZNO current                            [Amps]

  DATA   Pset   --  power setting                          [Megajoules/msec]
         Eset   --  energy setting                         [Megajoules]
         fdel   --  firing delay                           [msec]
         fdur   --  firing duration                        [msec]
 
  VAR  power    --  power into ZnO resistor                [Watts]
       trip     --  gap firing control signal              [0 or 1]
       energy   --  energy into ZnO resistor               [Joules]
       tfire    --  time at which the gap was last fired   [sec]
       vcap     --  voltage difference across series caps  [Volts] 

  OUTPUT  trip

  HISTORY  INTEGRAL(power) {DFLT:0}

  INIT trip:=0
       tfire:=0
  ENDINIT

  EXEC
    ------------------------------------------------------------------
    vcap:=V1-V2
    power:=vcap*iczn
    energy:=INTEGRAL(power)
    ------------------------------------------------------------------
    IF  trip>0              -- is already firing
    AND t-tfire>fdur*1.e-3  -- has exceeded firing duration
    THEN
      trip:=0     -- cancel the firing signal
      tfire:=0    -- null the firing time
    ENDIF
    ------------------------------------------------------------------
    IF trip=0                        -- is not signaling to fire
    AND tfire=0                      -- firing condition not yet detected
    AND (    power  >= Pset * 1.e9   -- power setting exceeded
          OR energy >= Eset * 1.e6 ) -- energy setting exceeded
    THEN
      tfire:=t    -- set the firing detection time
    ENDIF
    ------------------------------------------------------------------
    IF trip=0                 -- is not signaling to fire
    AND tfire>0               -- firing condition has been detected
    AND t-tfire>=fdel*1.e-3   -- firing delay exceeded
    THEN
      trip:=1     -- set the firing signal
    ENDIF
    ------------------------------------------------------------------
  ENDEXEC

ENDMODEL  

</datastring>
      </comp_content>
      <Model UseAs="Flash_1" />
    </comp>

            </icon>
            <datastring>MODEL FLUX3
DATA Freq
     Seq           -- 1: AB-BC-CA, 2: AC-BA-CB
     Tstart[1..3]  -- <0 initialize via imaginary value
INPUT V[1..3]  {dflt:0}  -- voltage node
      Vi[1..3] {dflt:0}  -- voltage node, imaginary part, connect together externally
OUTPUT Flux[1..3]
VAR Flux[1..3], omega, i, dV[1..3]
INIT
  Flux[1..3]:=0
  omega:=2*pi*Freq
ENDINIT  
HISTORY integral(dV[1]) {dflt:(Vi[1]-Vi[(Seq mod 3)+1])/omega*(Tstart[1]<0)}
HISTORY integral(dV[2]) {dflt:(Vi[2]-Vi[((1+Seq) mod 3)+1])/omega*(Tstart[2]<0)}
HISTORY integral(dV[3]) {dflt:(Vi[3]-Vi[((2+Seq) mod 3)+1])/Omega*(Tstart[3]<0)}
EXEC  
  for i:=1 to 3 do
    if (T>=Tstart[i]) then
      dV[i]:=V[i]-V[((i+Seq-1) mod 3)+1]      
      Flux[i]:=integral(dV[i])
    else
      integral(dV[i]):=0
    endif
  endfor
ENDEXEC
ENDMODEL</datastring>
          </comp_content>
          <Model UseAs="FLX3" />
        </comp>

<comp Name="MODELWRITE" Id="WRITEMAXMIN">
      <comp_content HighRes="false" Icon="default">
        <node Name="X" Value="" Kind="1" PosX="-20" PosY="0" NamePosX="-4" NamePosY="0" />
        <data Name="AsFuncOf" Unit="VAR" Value="0" />
        <data Name="MaxOrMin" Unit="1/0; 1=Max" Value="1" />
        <data Name="Tlimit" Unit="s" Value="0" />
        <data Name="Idx" Unit="Identifier" Value="1" />
        <datastring>MODEL WRITEMAXMIN
comment--------------------------------------------------------
| Special purpose Model.                                      |
| The output of this Model is written to the lis-file.        |
| The data Idx is used to identify the module in the lis-file.|
| The lis-file is automatically read after the simulation.    |
| Handles multiple run. If AsFuncOf is a number the           |
| simulation number is used instead.                          | 
-----------------------------------------------------endcomment
INPUT X
DATA 
  AsFuncOf --this can be an Variable. Used in the plotting x-axis
  MaxOrMin --if >0 the maximum with be stored, otherwise the minimum 
  Tlimit   --wait until this time to start looking for an extreme value.
  Idx      --unique identifier (managed by ATPDraw)
VAR xmin,xmax,xout
INIT
  xout:=0
  xmin:=inf
  xmax:=-inf
ENDINIT
EXEC
  if T>Tlimit
  then
    xmin:=min(xmin,x)
    xmax:=max(xmax,x)
    if MaxOrMin>0
    then
      xout:=xmax
    else 
      xout:=xmin
    endif
  endif
  if round(T/timestep)=round(stoptime/timestep)
  then 
    write('BEGIN WRITE @WRITEMAXMIN',trunc(Idx))    --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw
    write(xout,' ',AsFuncOf)                        --Add multiple columns or multiple lines 
    write('END WRITE @WRITEMAXMIN',trunc(Idx))      --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw
  endif
ENDEXEC
ENDMODEL </datastring>
      </comp_content>
      <Model UseAs="WRITEMAXMIN" />
    </comp>

\par   theta \{DFLT:theta0*PI/180\}
\par INIT
\par   omega0 := 2*PI*f0
\par   theta := theta0*PI/180.0
\par ENDINIT
\par EXEC
\par   -- From three-phase to alfa-beta-zero
\par   ualpha := SQRT(2/3)*(u[1] - 0.5*(u[2]+u[3]))
\par   ubeta := SQRT(0.5)*(u[2] - u[3])

\par   ubetaN := ubeta*temp
\par   -- From alfa-beta to d-q (with constant frequency)
\par   u_d := SQRT(2/3)*(ualpha*cos(theta) + ubeta*sin(theta))
\par   u_q := SQRT(2/3)*(-ualpha*sin(theta) + ubeta*cos(theta))
\par   uampl := SQRT(u_d*u_d+u_q*u_q)
\par   u_dN := ualfaN*cos(theta) + ubetaN*sin(theta)
\par   COMBINE ITERATE AS theta_comp
\par     u_qN := -ualfaN*sin(theta) + ubetaN*cos(theta)
\par     -- Phase-locked loop follows phase angle of the source
\par     CLAPLACE(wcon/u_qN) := (Gain|s0 + 0.001242|s1)/(1.0|s0 + 0.02315|s1)
\par     --CLAPLACE(wcon/u_qN) := (Gain|s0 + 4.0|s1)/(0.0|s0 + 1.0|s1)
\par     omega := omega0 + wcon
\par     theta := INTEGRAL(omega)

IEEE-PES Winter Meeting 2001,     pp. 1033-1038.    14-Aug-2005, Prof. M. Kizilcay========================================================== ENDCOMMENTINPUT  u[1..3]              -- phase voltagesOUTPUT FREQCONST  twopi  {VAL:6.283185307}DATA  theta0 {DFLT:0.0}          -- phase betw. d-axis and alpha-axis  f0     {DFLT:50.0}  Gain   {DFLT:22.85}VAR  ualpha, ubeta, u0, ualfaN, ubetaN,  u_dN, u_qN, u_d, u_q, uampl  theta, wcon   omega, omega0,freq   ucomp, tempHISTORY  wcon {DFLT:0}  u_qN {DFLT:0}  omega {DFLT:2*PI*f0}  INTEGRAL(omega) {DFLT:theta0*PI/180}  freq {DFLT:50}  theta {DFLT:theta0*PI/180}INIT  omega0 := 2*PI*f0  theta := theta0*PI/180.0ENDINITEXEC  -- From three-phase to alfa-beta-zero  ualpha := SQRT(2/3)*(u[1] - 0.5*(u[2]+u[3]))  ubeta := SQRT(0.5)*(u[2] - u[3])  u0 := (u[1] + u[2] + u[3])/3.0  temp := RECIP(SQRT(ualpha*ualpha+ubeta*ubeta))  ualfaN := ualpha*temp  ubetaN := ubeta*temp  -- From alfa-beta to d-q (with constant frequency)  u_d := SQRT(2/3)*(ualpha*cos(theta) + ubeta*sin(theta))  u_q := SQRT(2/3)*(-ualpha*sin(theta) + ubeta*cos(theta))  uampl := SQRT(u_d*u_d+u_q*u_q)  u_dN := ualfaN*cos(theta) + ubetaN*sin(theta)  COMBINE ITERATE AS theta_comp    u_qN := -ualfaN*sin(theta) + ubetaN*cos(theta)    -- Phase-locked loop follows phase angle of the source    CLAPLACE(wcon/u_qN) := (Gain|s0 + 0.001242|s1)/(1.0|s0 + 0.02315|s1)    --CLAPLACE(wcon/u_qN) := (Gain|s0 + 4.0|s1)/(0.0|s0 + 1.0|s1)    omega := omega0 + wcon    theta := INTEGRAL(omega)  ENDCOMBINE  FREQ := omega/twopi  ucomp := uampl*cos(theta)ENDEXECENDMODEL</datastring>

        <helpstring>{\rtf1\ansi\deff0{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Courier New;}}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\lang1044\f0\fs20 MODEL UI2PQ3
\par comment--------------------------------------------------------------
\par This model calculates the input active and reactive power of a time 
\par domain voltage/current signals by a user selectable algorithm
\par Algorithm=0: FFT Radix2-8. More robust 
\par Algorithm=1: DFT recursive. Faster, some drift. Handles sub-harmonics.
\par One period of the signal is needed to reach steady state. 
\par SampleFreq frequency should be a whole multiple of the power frequency.
\par -----------------------------------------------------------endcomment
\par INPUT 
\par   V[1..3], I[1..3]     --input signals to be transformed to phasors
\par DATA  
\par   FREQ \{DFLT:50\}       --power frequency
\par   SampleFreq \{dflt:400\}--sample frequency in this model in Hz
\par   ScaleV \{dflt:1\}      --multiply output by this number 
\par   ScaleI \{dflt:1\}      --multiply output by this number
\par   Algorithm \{dflt:0\}   --0: FFT radix2-8, 1: DFT recursive
\par OUTPUT 
\par   P, Q     --Active and reactive power output signals (rms)
\par VAR    
\par   P, Q, reV[1..3],imV[1..3],reI[1..3],imI[1..3],NSAMPL, OMEGA,
\par   D,alpha,x1,x3,x5,x7,xre,xim,n,delta_T[0..7]
\par 
\par HISTORY
\par   V[1..3] \{DFLT:0\}
\par   I[1..3] \{DFLT:0\}
\par timestep min: 1/SampleFreq
\par DELAY CELLS (V[1..3]) : recip(FREQ*timestep)+2
\par DELAY CELLS (I[1..3]) : recip(FREQ*timestep)+2
\par 
\par INIT 
\par   OMEGA:= 2*PI*FREQ
\par   NSAMPL:=recip(FREQ*timestep)
\par   reV[1..3] :=0
\par   imV[1..3] :=0
\par   reI[1..3] :=0
\par   imI[1..3] :=0
\par   alpha:=1/sqrt(2)
\par   for n:= 0 to 7 do
\par     delta_T[n] := n/(FREQ*8)
\par   endfor
\par ENDINIT
\par EXEC
\par   P:=0
\par   Q:=0
\par   for n:=1 to 3 do
\par     if Algorithm=0
\par     then
\par       x1 := delay(V[n],delta_T[0],1) - delay(V[n],delta_T[4],1)
\par       x3 := delay(V[n],delta_T[2],1) - delay(V[n],delta_T[6],1)
\par       x5 := delay(V[n],delta_T[1],1) - delay(V[n],delta_T[5],1)
\par       x7 := delay(V[n],delta_T[3],1) - delay(V[n],delta_T[7],1)
\par       xRe := x1 + (x5 - x7)*alpha
\par       xIm := x3 + (x5 + x7)*alpha
\par       ReV[n] := (xRe*cos(OMEGA*T)+xIm*sin(OMEGA*T))/4
\par       ImV[n] := (xIm*cos(OMEGA*T)-xRe*sin(OMEGA*T))/4
\par       x1 := delay(I[n],delta_T[0],1) - delay(I[n],delta_T[4],1)
\par       x3 := delay(I[n],delta_T[2],1) - delay(I[n],delta_T[6],1)
\par       x5 := delay(I[n],delta_T[1],1) - delay(I[n],delta_T[5],1)
\par       x7 := delay(I[n],delta_T[3],1) - delay(I[n],delta_T[7],1)
\par       xRe := x1 + (x5 - x7)*alpha
\par       xIm := x3 + (x5 + x7)*alpha
\par       ReI[n] := (xRe*cos(OMEGA*T)+xIm*sin(OMEGA*T))/4
\par       ImI[n] := (xIm*cos(OMEGA*T)-xRe*sin(OMEGA*T))/4
\par     else
\par       x1:=delay(V[n],1/FREQ,2)
\par       D:=2/NSAMPL*(V[n]-x1)*cos(OMEGA*T) 
\par       ReV[n]:=ReV[n]+D
\par       D:=2/NSAMPL*(V[n]-x1)*sin(OMEGA*T) 
\par       ImV[n]:=ImV[n]-D
\par       x1:=delay(I[n],1/FREQ,2)
\par       D:=2/NSAMPL*(I[n]-x1)*cos(OMEGA*T) 
\par       ReI[n]:=ReI[n]+D
\par       D:=2/NSAMPL*(I[n]-x1)*sin(OMEGA*T) 
\par       ImI[n]:=ImI[n]-D
\par     endif
\par     P:=P+(reV[n]*reI[n]+imV[n]*imI[n])*ScaleV*ScaleI/2
\par     Q:=Q+(imV[n]*reI[n]-reV[n]*imI[n])*ScaleV*ScaleI/2
\par   endfor
\par ENDEXEC
\par ENDMODEL
\par }

delay(V[n],delta_T[4],1)      x3 := delay(V[n],delta_T[2],1) - delay(V[n],delta_T[6],1)      x5 := delay(V[n],delta_T[1],1) - delay(V[n],delta_T[5],1)      x7 := delay(V[n],delta_T[3],1) - delay(V[n],delta_T[7],1)      xRe := x1 + (x5 - x7)*alpha      xIm := x3 + (x5 + x7)*alpha      ReV[n] := (xRe*cos(OMEGA*T)+xIm*sin(OMEGA*T))/4      ImV[n] := (xIm*cos(OMEGA*T)-xRe*sin(OMEGA*T))/4      x1 := delay(I[n],delta_T[0],1) - delay(I[n],delta_T[4],1)      x3 := delay(I[n],delta_T[2],1) -       <comp_content HighRes="false" Icon="default">
        <node Name="R" Value="" NumPhases="3" Kind="8" PosX="-20" PosY="-10" NamePosX="-4" NamePosY="-4" />
        <node Name="X" Value="" NumPhases="3" Kind="8" PosX="-20" PosY="10" NamePosX="-4" NamePosY="4" />

        <data Name="t_zone1" Unit="sec" Value="0" />
        <data Name="t_zone2" Unit="sec" Value="0.2" />

        <data Name="RC_z1" Unit="ohm" Value="-1" />
        <data Name="XC_z1" Unit="ohm" Value="-1" />

        <data Name="RC_z2" Unit="ohm" Value="-1" />
        <data Name="XC_z2" Unit="ohm" Value="-1" />
        <data Name="Radii_z2" Unit="ohm" Value="12" />
        <data Name="RC_z3" Unit="ohm" Value="1" />
        <data Name="XC_z3" Unit="ohm" Value="10" />
        <data Name="Radii_z3" Unit="ohm" Value="20" />
        <data Name="RL" Unit="ohm" Value="10" />

        <data Name="Idx" Unit="1..n" Value="1" />
        <helpstring>{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Courier New;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\lang1044\f0\fs20 MODEL W1RELAY21C 
\par 
\par COMMENT
\par Impedance element relay, 11.12.2014, by Hans Kr. H\'f8idalen
\par Impedance(distance) relay with circular characteristic. To be used together with R-X calculator model.
\par ENDCOMMENT
\par 
\par DATA 
\par   t_zone1\{dflt:0.2\} -- tripdelay zone 1 [s]
\par   t_zone2\{dflt:0.5\} -- tripdelay zone 2 [s]
\par   t_zone3\{dflt:1\}   -- tripdelay zone 3 [s]
\par  -- zone 1 characterstic parameters
\par   RC_z1\{dflt:-1\}    -- R coordinate centre zone 1, negative value means mho-charateristic
\par   XC_z1\{dflt:-1\}    -- X coordinate centre  zone 1
\par   Radii_z1\{dflt:8\}  -- Radius zone 1
\par  -- zone 2 characterstic parameters
\par   RC_z2\{dflt:-1\}    -- X coordinate centre zone 2
\par   XC_z2\{dflt:-1\}    -- R coordinate centre zone 2
\par   Radii_z2\{dflt:12\} -- Radius zone 2
\par  -- zone 3 characterstic parameters
\par   RC_z3\{dflt:-1\}    -- R coordinate centre zone 3
\par   XC_z3\{dflt:-1\}    -- X coordinate centre zone 3
\par   Radii_z3\{dflt:20\} -- Radius zone 2
\par    --Line impedance
\par   RL \{dflt:1\}       -- Real part of line impedance; for plotting and mho-characteristic
\par   XL \{dflt:10\}      -- Imaginary part of line impedance.
\par   DownSampl\{dflt:10\}-- Only record each DownSampl sample 
\par   t_init            -- Time before relay starts sampling
\par   Idx               -- Unique identifier (managed by ATPDraw)
\par 
\par INPUT 
\par   R[1..3] -- [Ohm]
\par   X[1..3] -- [Ohm]
\par   Block \{DFLT:0\} -- [1:block, 0:unblock) 
\par  
\par OUTPUT 
\par   Trip  -- 1 IF trip
\par   Zone[1..3] -- Outputs which zone trips in the three phases 1..3 as function of time     
\par 
\par VAR 
\par   Trip, zone[1..3], startZ1[1..3], startZ2[1..3], startZ3[1..3],i,k, alpha
\par   R1,R2,R3,X1,X2,X3
\par   timeZ1[1..3] -- timer zone 1
\par   timeZ2[1..3] -- timer zone 2
\par   timeZ3[1..3] -- timer zone 3    
\par INIT
\par   trip:=1
\par   zone[1..3]:=0
\par   timeZ1[1..3]:=0
\par   timeZ2[1..3]:=0
\par   timeZ3[1..3]:=0
\par   startZ1[1..3]:=0
\par   startZ2[1..3]:=0
\par   startZ3[1..3]:=0
\par   k:=0
\par   alpha:=atan2(XL,RL)
\par   if RC_z1<0
\par   then

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\lang1044\f0\fs20 MODEL W1RELAY21P 
\par 
\par COMMENT
\par Impedance element relay, 11.06.2012,
\par by Torstein Stadheim
\par 
\par Impedance(distance) relay with polygon characteristic. To be used together with R-X calculator model.
\par The model are using the principle of convex polygons to check IF a point is inside a polygon. For this model to work, the points should be defined counter-clockwise, and no vector from point n to point n+1 should cross another point(m)-to-point(m+1) vector.
\par 
\par The polygons should be defined in the following manner:
\par                          |X
\par                    3-----|------2
\par                    | 3---|---2  | etc...
\par                    | |   |   |  |
\par                    | |   |   |  |
\par -----------------------------------------------------> R
\par                    | |   |   |  |
\par                    | 4---|---1  | ZONE 1 INNERMOST
\par                    |     |      |
\par                    4-----|------1
\par                          |
\par Sources:\tab http://erich.realtimerendering.com/ptinpoly/
\par 
\par 3-phase model by HK H\'f8idalen, 2012
\par 
\par ENDCOMMENT
\par 
\par -- positive IF a point(x,y) is on the left side of vector [x2-x1,y2-y1], starting at (x1,y1)
\par FUNCTION check(x,y,x1,y1,x2,y2) := ((x2-x1)*(y-y1))-((x-x1)*(y2-y1))
\par 
\par DATA\tab t_zone1\{dflt:0.2\}\tab -- tripdelay zone 1 [s]
\par \tab t_zone2\{dflt:0.5\}\tab -- tripdelay zone 2 [s]
\par \tab t_zone3\{dflt:1\}\tab -- tripdelay zone 3 [s]
\par \tab -- zone 1 characterstic parameters; clock-counterwise orientation of polygon
\par \tab R1_z1\{dflt:1\}\tab -- R coordinate point.1 zone 1
\par \tab X1_z1\{dflt:-1\}\tab -- X coordinate point.1 zone 1
\par \tab R2_z1\{dflt:1\}\tab -- R coordinate point.2 zone 1
\par \tab X2_z1\{dflt:1\}\tab -- X coordinate point.2 zone 1
\par \tab R3_z1\{dflt:-1\}\tab -- R coordinate point.3 zone 1
\par \tab X3_z1\{dflt:1\}\tab -- X coordinate point.3 zone 1
\par \tab R4_z1\{dflt:-1\}\tab -- R coordinate point.4 zone 1
\par \tab X4_z1\{dflt:-1\}\tab -- X coordinate point.4 zone 1
\par \tab --zone 2 characterstic parameters
\par \tab R1_z2\{dflt:2\}\tab -- R coordinate point.1 zone 2
\par \tab X1_z2\{dflt:-2\}\tab -- X coordinate point.1 zone 2
\par \tab R2_z2\{dflt:2\}\tab -- R coordinate point.2 zone 2
\par \tab X2_z2\{dflt:2\}\tab -- X coordinate point.2 zone 2
\par \tab R3_z2\{dflt:-2\}\tab -- R coordinate point.3 zone 2
\par \tab X3_z2\{dflt:2\}\tab -- X coordinate point.3 zone 2
\par \tab R4_z2\{dflt:-2\}\tab -- R coordinate point.4 zone 2
\par \tab X4_z2\{dflt:-2\}\tab -- X coordinate point.4 zone 2
\par \tab --zone 3 characterstic parameters
\par \tab R1_z3\{dflt:3\}\tab -- R coordinate point.1 zone 3
\par \tab X1_z3\{dflt:-3\}\tab -- X coordinate point.1 zone 3
\par \tab R2_z3\{dflt:3\}\tab -- R coordinate point.2 zone 3
\par \tab X2_z3\{dflt:3\}\tab -- X coordinate point.2 zone 3
\par \tab R3_z3\{dflt:-3\}\tab -- R coordinate point.3 zone 3
\par \tab X3_z3\{dflt:3\}\tab -- X coordinate point.3 zone 3
\par \tab R4_z3\{dflt:-3\}\tab -- R coordinate point.4 zone 3
\par \tab X4_z3\{dflt:-3\}\tab -- X coordinate point.4 zone 3
\par       --Line impedance
\par       RL\{dflt:1\}        -- Real part of line impedance; for plotting 
\par       XL\{dflt:10\}       -- Imaginary part of line impedance.
\par       DownSampl\{dflt:10\}-- Only record each DownSampl sample 
\par       t_init            -- Time before relay starts sampling
\par       Idx               --unique identifier (managed by ATPDraw)
\par 
\par INPUT\tab R[1..3]\tab -- [Ohm]
\par \tab X[1..3]\tab -- [Ohm]
\par \tab Block       \{DFLT:0\} -- [1:block, 0:unblock)\tab 
\par 
\par OUTPUT Trip\tab\tab -- 1 IF trip
\par        Zone[1..3] -- Outputs which zone trips in the three phases 1..3 as function of time     
\par 
\par VAR\tab Trip
\par       zone[1..3]
\par \tab startZ1[1..3]
\par \tab startZ2[1..3]
\par \tab startZ3[1..3]
\par \tab timeZ1[1..3]\tab -- timer zone 1
\par \tab timeZ2[1..3]\tab -- timer zone 2
\par \tab timeZ3[1..3]\tab -- timer zone 3
\par       i,k      
\par INIT
\par \tab trip:=1
\par       zone[1..3]:=0
\par \tab timeZ1[1..3]:=0
\par \tab timeZ2[1..3]:=0
\par \tab timeZ3[1..3]:=0
\par \tab startZ1[1..3]:=0
\par \tab startZ2[1..3]:=0
\par \tab startZ3[1..3]:=0
\par       k:=0
\par 
\par ENDINIT
\par EXEC
\par   if (t>t_init) and (Block=false)
\par   then
\par   FOR i:=1 to 3 DO
\par -------------------------check IF inside zone 3-----------
\par     IF check(R[i],X[i],R1_z3,X1_z3,R2_z3,X2_z3) > 0 AND
\par \tab  check(R[i],X[i],R2_z3,X2_z3,R3_z3,X3_z3) > 0 AND
\par \tab  check(R[i],X[i],R3_z3,X3_z3,R4_z3,X4_z3) > 0 AND
\par \tab  check(R[i],X[i],R4_z3,X4_z3,R1_z3,X1_z3) > 0 
\par     THEN
\par \tab startZ3[i] := 1 -- inside zone 3
\par \tab timeZ3[i] := timeZ3[i] + timestep
\par     ELSE -- outside zone 3
\par \tab startZ3[i] := 0
\par \tab timeZ3[i] := 0
\par \tab startZ2[i] := 0
\par \tab timeZ2[i] := 0
\par \tab startZ1[i] := 0
\par \tab timeZ1[i] := 0
\par     ENDIF
\par \tab\tab

\par -- does not check zone 2 IF point is outside zone 3
\par     IF startZ3[i]=1 AND
\par        check(R[i],X[i],R1_z2,X1_z2,R2_z2,X2_z2) > 0 AND
\par \tab  check(R[i],X[i],R2_z2,X2_z2,R3_z2,X3_z2) > 0 AND
\par \tab  check(R[i],X[i],R3_z2,X3_z2,R4_z2,X4_z2) > 0 AND
\par \tab  check(R[i],X[i],R4_z2,X4_z2,R1_z2,X1_z2) > 0 
\par     THEN
\par \tab startZ2[i] := 1 -- inside zone 2
\par \tab timeZ2[i] := timeZ2[i] + timestep
\par     ELSE -- outside zone 2
\par \tab startZ2[i] := 0
\par \tab timeZ2[i] := 0
\par \tab startZ1[i] := 0
\par \tab timeZ1[i] := 0
\par     ENDIF
\par 
\par -------------------------check IF inside zone 1-----------------
\par -- does not check zone 1 IF point is outside zone 2
\par     IF startZ2[i] = 1 AND 
\par        check(R[i],X[i],R1_z1,X1_z1,R2_z1,X2_z1) > 0 AND 
\par \tab  check(R[i],X[i],R2_z1,X2_z1,R3_z1,X3_z1) > 0 AND
\par \tab  check(R[i],X[i],R3_z1,X3_z1,R4_z1,X4_z1) > 0 AND
\par \tab  check(R[i],X[i],R4_z1,X4_z1,R1_z1,X1_z1) > 0 
\par     THEN
\par \tab startZ1[i] := 1 -- inside zone 1
\par \tab timeZ1[i] := timeZ1[i] + timestep
\par     ELSE -- outside zone 1
\par \tab startZ1[i] := 0
\par \tab timeZ1[i] := 0
\par     ENDIF
\par 
\par 
\par ------------Check delay, and trip of timer runs out-----------------------------
\par     IF startZ3[i] = 0 THEN -- reset function
\par \tab zone[i] := 0
\par     ELSIF\tab timeZ3[i] > t_zone3 THEN -- trip zone 3
\par \tab zone[i] := 3
\par     ELSIF timeZ2[i] > t_zone2 THEN -- trip zone 2
\par \tab zone[i] := 2
\par     ELSIF timeZ1[i] > t_zone1 THEN -- trip zone 1
\par \tab zone[i] := 1
\par     ENDIF
\par   ENDFOR
\par   trip:=not OR(zone[1],zone[2],zone[3],not trip)
\par 
\par   if (k mod DownSampl) = 0
\par   then

\par     write(R[1],X[1],R[2],X[2],R[3],X[3],trip,T)    --Add multiple columns or multiple lines 
\par     write('END WRITE @W1RELAY21P',round(Idx))      --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw
\par   endif 
\par   k:=k+1
\par   endif
\par ENDEXEC
\par ENDMODEL
\par 
\par 
\par 
\par 
\par }

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\lang1044\f0\fs20 MODEL W1RELAY27
\par comment------------------------------------------------------------
\par Constant time, two-step undervoltage relay with definite time and 
\par inverse time delay characteristics
\par TYPE A: t = K/((Uthreshold - Urms)/Uthreshold)
\par 
\par TYPE B: t = 480*K/(32*(Uthreshold - Urms)/Uthreshold - 0.5)^2.0 + 0.05
\par 
\par Used with RMS model or FFT/DFT model for processing the input signal. 
\par As the RMS model gives outputs only after a periods time, this is 
\par considered and the relay does not operate in any way before one 
\par time period has passed. 
\par 
\par ---------------------------------------------------------endcomment
\par DATA 
\par   Ubase \{dflt:10\}    -- Base voltage (primary side of VT) [kV]
\par   Uth1  \{dflt:80\}    -- threshold voltage for step 1 in percent of Ubase
\par   Uth2  \{dflt:50\}    -- threshold voltage for step 2 in percent of Ubase
\par   t_delay1 \{dflt:1\}  -- time delay for step 1
\par   t_delay2 \{dflt:0.2\}  -- time delay for step 2
\par   IDMT1  \{dflt:0\}    -- type of inverse time characteristic for step 1, 0= none, 1= Type A, 2= Type B
\par   IDMT2  \{dflt:0\}    -- type of inverse time characteristic for step 2, 0= none, 1= Type A, 2= Type B
\par   K1  \{dflt:0.05\}    -- time multiplier setting for step 1, (0.05 - 1.10) in steps of 0.001
\par   K2  \{dflt:0.05\}    -- time multiplier setting for step 2, (0.05 - 1.10) in steps of 0.001
\par   t_init \{dflt:0.02\} -- Time before relay starts sampling
\par   DownSampl \{dflt:0\} -- Store only every DownSample points 
\par   Idx                -- Unique identifier managed by ATPDraw     
\par INPUT 
\par   Urms[1..3]         -- Input signal (rms value)
\par   block \{dflt:0\}
\par OUTPUT 
\par   trip, zone[1..3]
\par VAR trip, trip1[1..3], trip2[1..3], t1[1..3], t2[1..3], td1, td2, zone[1..3], n
\par     Uth1V,Uth2V,k,tmax[1..3],Ub
\par INIT
\par   trip:= 1
\par   trip1[1..3]:= 0
\par   trip2[1..3]:= 0
\par   t1[1..3]:= 0 -- timer 1
\par   t2[1..3]:= 0 -- timer 2
\par   td1:= 0
\par   td1:= 0 
\par   zone[1..3]:= 0 -- Faulted phase(s) represented by 1
\par   Ub:=Ubase*1000/sqrt(3)   --phase voltage in [V]
\par   Uth1V:=Ub*Uth1/100 
\par   Uth2V:=Ub*Uth2/100
\par   k:=0
\par ENDINIT
\par 
\par EXEC
\par   IF (t > t_init) AND (Block=FALSE) 
\par   THEN
\par     FOR n:=1 TO 3 DO   -- run through all three phases
\par       IF IDMT1 = 0 THEN   -- select time delay characteristic
\par         td1:= t_delay1
\par       ELSIF IDMT1 = 1 THEN
\par         td1:= K1*recip(1-Urms[n]/Uth1V)
\par       ELSIF IDMT1 = 2 THEN
\par         td1:= K1*480*recip((32*(1-Urms[n]/Uth1V)-0.5)**2)+0.055
\par       ENDIF
\par 
\par       IF IDMT2 = 0 THEN
\par         td2:= t_delay2
\par       ELSIF IDMT2 = 1 THEN
\par         td2:= K2*recip(1-Urms[n]/Uth2V)
\par       ELSIF IDMT2 = 2 THEN
\par         td2:= K2*480*recip((32*(1-Urms[n]/Uth2V)-0.5)**2)+0.055
\par       ENDIF
\par       -- step 1
\par       IF ABS(Urms[n]) <= Uth1V
\par       THEN   
\par         IF t1[n] >= td1 THEN
\par           trip1[n]:= 1
\par         ELSE
\par           trip1[n]:= 0
\par         ENDIF 
\par         t1[n]:= t1[n] + timestep
\par       ELSE
\par         t1[n]:=0
\par         trip1[n]:=0
\par       ENDIF
\par       -- step 2
\par       IF Urms[n] <= Uth2V THEN
\par         t2[n]:= t2[n]+ timestep
\par         IF t2[n]>= td2 THEN
\par           trip2[n]:= 1
\par         ELSE
\par           trip2[n]:= 0
\par         ENDIF
\par       ELSE
\par         t2[n]:=0
\par         trip2[n]:=0
\par       ENDIF
\par       zone[n]:= trip1[n] OR trip2[n]
\par       tmax[n]:=max(t1[n],t2[n])
\par     ENDFOR
\par     trip:= not OR(zone[1], zone[2], zone[3], not trip)
\par     if (k mod DownSampl) = 0
\par     then
\par       write('BEGIN WRITE @W1RELAY27',round(Idx))    --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw
\par       write(Urms[1]/Ub,tmax[1],Urms[2]/Ub,tmax[2],Urms[3]/Ub,tmax[3],trip,T)    --Add multiple columns or multiple lines 
\par       write('END WRITE @W1RELAY27',round(Idx))      --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw
\par     endif 
\par     k:=k+1
\par   ENDIF
\par ENDEXEC
\par ENDMODEL
\par }
</helpstring>

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\lang1044\f0\fs20 MODEL W1RELAY51I
\par comment------------------------------------------------------------
\par   Inverse time overcurrent relay.
\par   ts= D*(A/((Irms/Is)^Q -1 )+B)
\par ---------------------------------------------------------endcomment
\par DATA Is  --Starting current
\par      D   --time multiplier
\par      -- IEC:  NI    VI    EI   IEEE:    NI     VI     EI
\par      A  --  0.14  13.5  80.0        0.0515  19.61  28.20 
\par      B  --    0      0     0        0.1140  0.491 0.1217           
\par      Q  -- 0.02      1     2          0.02      2      2

\par      t_init     -- Time before relay starts sampling
\par      Idx        -- Unique identifier (managed by ATPDraw)
\par INPUT 
\par   irms[1..3]
\par   Block \{dflt:0\}-- Blocking signal TRUE or 1 = Block
\par OUTPUT Trip
\par        Zone[1..3] --Shows which zone (0 or 1 here) trips in which phase (1..3) 
\par VAR trip,Zone[1..3],ts[1..3],M,j,n
\par INIT
\par   trip:=1
\par   Zone[1..3]:=0  
\par   ts[1..3]:=0
\par   j:=0

\par     write('END WRITE @W1RELAY51I',round(Idx))                    --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw

        <datastring>MODEL W1RELAY51Icomment------------------------------------------------------------  Inverse time overcurrent relay.  ts= D*(A/((Irms/Is)^Q -1 )+B)---------------------------------------------------------endcommentDATA Is  --Starting current     D   --time multiplier     -- IEC:  NI    VI    EI   IEEE:    NI     VI     EI     A  --  0.14  13.5  80.0        0.0515  19.61  28.20      B  --    0      0     0        0.1140  0.491 0.1217                Q  -- 0.02      1     2          0.02      2      2      Tr --                            4.85   21.6   29.1     DownSampl  -- Write out every DownSampl     t_init     -- Time before relay starts sampling     Idx        -- Unique identifier (managed by ATPDraw)INPUT   irms[1..3]  Block {dflt:0}-- Blocking signal TRUE or 1 = BlockOUTPUT Trip       Zone[1..3] --Shows which zone (0 or 1 here) trips in which phase (1..3) VAR trip,Zone[1..3],ts[1..3],M,j,nINIT  trip:=1  Zone[1..3]:=0    ts[1..3]:=0  j:=0ENDINITEXEC  if (t>t_init) and (Block=FALSE)  then   FOR n:=1 TO 3 DO    M:=ABS(Irms[n]*recip(Is))    if M>1    then      ts[n]:=ts[n]+timestep      if ts[n]>D*(A*recip(M**Q-1)+B)      then        Zone[n]:=1      endif    else      ts[n]:=ts[n]-timestep      if ts[n]<-D*Tr*recip(M**2-1)      then        ts[n]:=0      endif    endif  ENDFOR  trip:=not OR(Zone[1],Zone[2],Zone[3],not trip)  if (j mod DownSampl) = 0  then    write('BEGIN WRITE @W1RELAY51I',round(Idx))                  --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw    write(Irms[1], ts[1], Irms[2], ts[2], Irms[3], ts[3], trip)  --Add multiple columns or multiple lines     write('END WRITE @W1RELAY51I',round(Idx))                    --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw  endif   j:=j+1  endifENDEXECENDMODEL</datastring>

    </comp>

        <datastring>MODEL W1RELAY59comment------------------------------------------------------------Constant time, two-step overvoltage relay with definite time and inverse time delay characteristicsTYPE A: t = K/((Uthreshold - Urms)/Uthreshold)TYPE B: t = 480*K/(32*(Uthreshold - Urms)/Uthreshold - 0.5)^2.0 + 0.05Used with RMS model or FFT/DFT model for processing the input signal. As the RMS model gives outputs only after a periods time, this is considered and the relay does not operate in any way before one time period has passed. ---------------------------------------------------------endcommentDATA   Ubase {dflt:10}    -- Base voltage (primary side of VT) [kV]  Uth1  {dflt:110}    -- threshold voltage for step 1 in percent of Ubase  Uth2  {dflt:120}    -- threshold voltage for step 2 in percent of Ubase  t_delay1 {dflt:1}  -- time delay for step 1  t_delay2 {dflt:0.2}  -- time delay for step 2  IDMT1  {dflt:0}    -- type of inverse time characteristic for step 1, 0= none, 1= Type A, 2= Type B  IDMT2  {dflt:0}    -- type of inverse time characteristic for step 2, 0= none, 1= Type A, 2= Type B  K1  {dflt:0.05}    -- time multiplier setting for step 1, (0.05 - 1.10) in steps of 0.001  K2  {dflt:0.05}    -- time multiplier setting for step 2, (0.05 - 1.10) in steps of 0.001  t_init {dflt:0.02} -- Time before relay starts sampling  DownSampl {dflt:1} -- Store only every DownSampl point  Idx                -- Unique identifier managed by ATPDraw INPUT   Urms[1..3]         -- Input signal (rms value)  block {dflt:0}OUTPUT   trip, zone[1..3]VAR trip, trip1[1..3], trip2[1..3], t1[1..3], t2[1..3], td1, td2, zone[1..3], n    Uth1V,Uth2V,k,tmax[1..3],UbINIT  trip:= 1  trip1[1..3]:= 0  trip2[1..3]:= 0  t1[1..3]:= 0 -- timer 1  t2[1..3]:= 0 -- timer 2  td1:= 0  td1:= 0   zone[1..3]:= 0 -- Faulted phase(s) represented by 1  Ub:=Ubase*1000/sqrt(3)   --phase voltage in [V]  Uth1V:=Ub*Uth1/100   Uth2V:=Ub*Uth2/100  k:=0ENDINITEXEC  IF (t > t_init) AND (Block=FALSE)   THEN    FOR n:=1 TO 3 DO   -- run through all three phases      IF IDMT1 = 0 THEN   -- select time delay characteristic        td1:= t_delay1      ELSIF IDMT1 = 1 THEN        td1:= K1*recip(1-Urms[n]/Uth1V)      ELSIF IDMT1 = 2 THEN        td1:= K1*480*recip((32*(1-Urms[n]/Uth1V)-0.5)**2)+0.055      ENDIF      IF IDMT2 = 0 THEN        td2:= t_delay2      ELSIF IDMT2 = 1 THEN        td2:= K2*recip(1-Urms[n]/Uth2V)      ELSIF IDMT2 = 2 THEN        td2:= K2*480*recip((32*(1-Urms[n]/Uth2V)-0.5)**2)+0.055      ENDIF      -- step 1      IF ABS(Urms[n]) > Uth1V      THEN           IF t1[n] >= td1 THEN          trip1[n]:= 1        ELSE          trip1[n]:= 0        ENDIF         t1[n]:= t1[n] + timestep      ELSE        t1[n]:=0        trip1[n]:=0      ENDIF      -- step 2      IF Urms[n] > Uth2V THEN        t2[n]:= t2[n]+ timestep        IF t2[n]>= td2 THEN          trip2[n]:= 1        ELSE          trip2[n]:= 0        ENDIF      ELSE        t2[n]:=0        trip2[n]:=0      ENDIF      zone[n]:= trip1[n] OR trip2[n]      tmax[n]:=max(t1[n],t2[n])    ENDFOR    trip:= not OR(zone[1], zone[2], zone[3], not trip)    if (k mod DownSampl) = 0    then      write('BEGIN WRITE @W1RELAY59',round(Idx))    --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw      write(Urms[1]/Ub,tmax[1],Urms[2]/Ub,tmax[2],Urms[3]/Ub,tmax[3],trip,T)    --Add multiple columns or multiple lines       write('END WRITE @W1RELAY59',round(Idx))      --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw    endif     k:=k+1  ENDIFENDEXECENDMODEL</datastring>

        <datastring>MODEL W1RELAY67N
COMMENT
Calculates the phasors of the zero-sequence current and voltage 
Algorithm=0: 8-point RADIX-2 FFT algorithm for calculating phasor of specified frequency,
Algorithm=1: Recursive DFT algorithm. Faster, but more drift 
Trips is V0>Vlim and I0>Ilim and in correct sector set by PhiA and PhiB (with V0 real) 
after a delay td. Output a second close signal (closeV) when V0>Vlim
by Hans Kr. Høidalen, 01.03.2016
ENDCOMMENT
DATA
  VN         {dflt:22} -- System voltage in kV p-p rms.
  FREQ       {dflt:50} -- Frequency of the first harmonic
  Vlim       {dflt:5}  -- Zero-sequence treshold voltage in%
  Is         {dflt:5}  -- Zero-sequence pickup current in A
  PhiA       {dflt:30} -- Lower boundary trip sector in deg
  PhiB       {dflt:150}-- Upper boundary trip sector in deg
  td         {dflt:5}  -- Time delay in sec.
  tdaux      {dflt:1.5}-- Time delay of auxiliary output when V>Vlim
  SampleFreq {dflt:400}-- Sample frequency of relay (SampleFreq/FREQ integer >=8)
  ScaleI     {dflt:1}  -- Current multiplied by this value
  ScaleV     {dflt:1}  -- Voltage multiplied by this value
  Algorithm  {dflt:0}  -- 0: FFT8, 1:DFT recursive
  DownSampl  {dflt:1}  -- Print-out frequency
  t_init     {dflt:0.02} --Initial time delay before trip calculation starts ~1/FREQ
  Idx        --ModelWrite identifier
INPUT
  I[1..3]    -- Input 3-phase currents
  V[1..3]    -- Input 3-phase voltages
  Block      {dflt:0}
OUTPUT
  trip       -- trip signal to CB
  CloseAux   -- close auxilliary signal when V0>Vlim (to parallel resistance for instance)
VAR
  trip,CloseAux,I0,V0,reI0,imI0,reV0,imV0,OMEGA,NSAMPL,alpha,D,delta_T[0..7]
  x1,x3,x5,x7,xre,xim,tt,taux,k,Iabs,Vabs,reI0p,imI0p,delta,D
TIMESTEP min:recip(SampleFreq)
DELAY CELLS (I0,V0): recip(FREQ*timestep)+2 -- Need at least one first harmonic periode of sampling
HISTORY I0 {DFLT:0}, V0 {DFLT:0} -- Fills the signal with zeroes when time <= 0
INIT
  trip:=1
  CloseAux:=0
  FOR k:= 0 TO 7 DO
    delta_T[k] := k/(FREQ*8)
  ENDFOR
  alpha:=1/sqrt(2)
  OMEGA:=2*PI*FREQ 
  NSAMPL:=recip(FREQ*timestep)
  if abs(NSAMPL-trunc(NSAMPL))>1e-9
  then
    write('%%%WARNING in W1RELAY67N: SAMPLEFREQ/FREQ is not an integer number')
  endif 
  reI0 :=0
  imI0 :=0
  reV0 :=0
  imV0 :=0
  tt:=0
  taux:=0
  k:=0
ENDINIT
EXEC
if (t>t_init) and (Block=false)
then
  I0 := (I[1]+I[2]+I[3])/3
  V0 := (V[1]+V[2]+V[3])/3
  if Algorithm =0  --FFT Radix-2 8 levels
  then
    x1 := delay(I0,delta_T[0],1) - delay(I0,delta_T[4],1)
    x3 := delay(I0,delta_T[2],1) - delay(I0,delta_T[6],1)
    x5 := delay(I0,delta_T[1],1) - delay(I0,delta_T[5],1)
    x7 := delay(I0,delta_T[3],1) - delay(I0,delta_T[7],1)
    xre := x1 + (x5 - x7)*alpha
    xim := x3 + (x5 + x7)*alpha  
    reI0 := (xre*cos(OMEGA*T)+xim*sin(OMEGA*T))/4*ScaleI  --this moving window correction not needed in RX and PQ calc.
    imI0 := (xim*cos(OMEGA*T)-xre*sin(OMEGA*T))/4*ScaleI
    x1 := delay(V0,delta_T[0],1) - delay(V0,delta_T[4],1)
    x3 := delay(V0,delta_T[2],1) - delay(V0,delta_T[6],1)
    x5 := delay(V0,delta_T[1],1) - delay(V0,delta_T[5],1)
    x7 := delay(V0,delta_T[3],1) - delay(V0,delta_T[7],1)
    xre := x1 + (x5 - x7)*alpha
    xim := x3 + (x5 + x7)*alpha  
    reV0 := (xre*cos(OMEGA*T)+xim*sin(OMEGA*T))/4*ScaleV --this moving window correction not needed in RX and PQ calc.
    imV0 := (xim*cos(OMEGA*T)-xre*sin(OMEGA*T))/4*ScaleV
  else  --DFT recursive moving window ab-approach?    
    x1:=delay(V0,1/FREQ,2)
    D:=2/NSAMPL*(V0-x1)*cos(OMEGA*T) 
    reV0:=reV0+D
    D:=2/NSAMPL*(V0-x1)*sin(OMEGA*T) 
    imV0:=imV0-D
    x1:=delay(I0,1/FREQ,2)
    D:=2/NSAMPL*(I0-x1)*cos(OMEGA*T) 
    reI0:=reI0+D
    D:=2/NSAMPL*(I0-x1)*sin(OMEGA*T) 
    imI0:=imI0-D
  endif
  delta:=atan2(imI0,reI0)-atan2(imV0,reV0)
  Iabs:=sqrt(reI0**2+imI0**2)
  Vabs:=sqrt(reV0**2+imV0**2)
  reI0p:=Iabs*cos(delta)
  imI0p:=Iabs*sin(delta)
  delta:=delta*180/PI
  if Vabs>Vlim*VN*10/sqrt(3)
  then
    taux:=taux+timestep
    if taux>tdaux
    then

      CloseAux:=1
    endif
    if (Iabs>Is) and (delta>PhiA) and (delta<PhiB)
    then
      tt:=tt+timestep
      if tt>td
      then
        Trip:=0
        CloseAux:=0 --disconnect?
      endif
    else
      tt:=0
    endif
  else
   taux:=0
  endif
  if (k mod DownSampl) = 0
  then
    write('BEGIN WRITE @W1RELAY67N',round(Idx))    --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw
    write(reI0p,imI0p,trip,T)                      --Add multiple columns or multiple lines 
    write('END WRITE @W1RELAY67N',round(Idx))      --Do not modify this line, replaced by ATPDraw
  endif 
  k:=k+1
endif
ENDEXEC
ENDMODEL</datastring>

    </comp>

\par INIT

\par ENDMODEL
\par }
